No processes are currently running on port 5001. Here are the commands you can use in the future to kill a process on port 5001:

## Method 1: Find and kill by port (PowerShell/CMD)
```powershell
# Find the process using port 5001
netstat -ano | findstr :5001

# Then kill using the PID (replace XXXX with the actual PID from above)
taskkill /PID XXXX /F
```

## Method 2: One-liner to kill all processes on port 5001 (PowerShell)
```powershell
Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 5001 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.OwningProcess -Force }
```

## Method 3: Using netstat and taskkill in one command (CMD/PowerShell)
```cmd
for /f "tokens=5" %a in ('netstat -ano ^| findstr :5001') do taskkill /PID %a /F
```

## Common development server processes to check:
- **Node.js servers** typically run on ports like 3000, 5000, 5001, etc.
- **Python Flask/Django** servers often use 5000, 5001, 8000, etc.

Since no process is currently using port 5001, you should be able to start any service on that port without issues. If you encounter port conflicts in the future, use any of the commands above to free up the port.


If you must use 5001, run these in an elevated PowerShell (Run as Administrator):
```powershell
# Check if 5001 is in excluded TCP port ranges (requires admin)
netsh interface ipv4 show excludedportrange protocol=tcp | findstr 5001

# Check if an HTTP URL reservation exists (rarely needed for Express)
netsh http show urlacl | findstr :5001
```
If 5001 shows up in excluded ranges, pick another port (e.g., 5051) or adjust your system reservation. If it doesn’t, try:
```powershell
# Sometimes resolves EACCES on certain Windows configs
netsh http add urlacl url=http://+:5001/ user=Everyone
```

- If the backend starts on 5051, point your clients/tests to `http://localhost:5051`.
